title: Catherine de Medicis to Bernardin Bochetel, bishop of Rennes, 31 July 1563

documents.route: camp before Le Havre -> imperial court (Vienna)

plaintext.source: La Ferriere printed the letter (Lettres de Catherine de Medicis II, pp. 79-81) but set the ciphered block as '[ ]' with the footnote 'Partie chiffree'; Tomokiyo lists f. 55 as undeciphered.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, ark btv1b9059845t view 36, native 8720x5935
transcription.notes: Thirteen ciphered lines between the clear 'c'est pour' and the clear 'Au demourant'. Transcribed glyph by glyph from region crops at native resolution; token boundaries are mine. Several r/s, e/o and l/t homophones are near identical in this hand and remain uncertain, chiefly on lines 2, 4, 8, 12 and 13. Re-transcribed 21 Sept 2026 as f55_v2.txt (402 tokens, candidate-annotated; measured).

plaintext.source: Tomokiyo: 'not deciphered'; not printed in La Ferrière.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, ark btv1b9059845t view 36, native 8720x5935
transcription.notes: 15 cipher lines below a clear opening; glyph tokens with candidate values.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, ark btv1b9059845t view 36, native 8720x5935
transcription.notes: 14 faint cipher lines, many nulls; transcribed from contrast-enhanced crops; p.138 facing is glossed in the same hand.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, ark btv1b9059845t view 36, native 8720x5935
transcription.notes: About 25 cipher lines; clear end of the letter on p.232.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on invented signs, two to eight per letter, with about thirty word-signs and a set of nulls that includes ordinary French words written in clear.

diacritics.note: an overbar distinguishes homophones, e.g. 10 (i) from 10-bar (i), and marks the word-signs que (q-q bar), qui (V bar), la (mn bar).

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction of the Bishop of Rennes' cipher 1561-1564 (cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/henryiii.htm, images/CharlesIX_Rennes.png), built from the glossed letters of 500 Colbert 390 and BnF fr. 3158 f. 1; used.
system.notes: Nulls include the clear French words que, est, pour, plus, xix, vre, do, fo, written in line so the page reads as if partly in clear. l'Empereur and Roy de Boheme have their own signs.

prior_solution.where: La Ferriere (1885) prints the letter with the ciphered block left blank as 'Partie chiffree'; Tomokiyo marks f. 55 undeciphered while publishing a reconstructed key for the cipher. Tomokiyo held the key, so an unpublished reading may exist; 'undeciphered' on cryptiana means no contemporary decipherment.

conditions.human_role: set the target and the order of work; supplied no images, transcription or reading.

solution.what: Identified the four target items and their Gallica arks and views; fetched page images.
Copied Tomokiyo's reconstructed Rennes key (1561-1564) into key.md as an ASCII glyph table.
First attempt to transcribe f. 55 from 2500-px page images.

Located the letter in La Ferriere, Lettres de Catherine de Medicis II, pp. 79-81: the clear text on both sides of the cipher matches the page, and the ciphered block is printed as '[ ]' with the footnote 'Partie chiffree'. Confirms the passage was never read.
Re-fetched images at native resolution by IIIF region request (8720x5935); corrected fetch.py's stale view numbers for fr. 3181 (folio = view + 19, so f. 55 = view 36).

Calibrated the key on this scribe's shapes against the line-by-line margin decipherment of the sibling letter f. 57 (13 Aug 1563, view 38); its first ciphered line reads 'que les princes', fixing p, r, i, n, c and e.
Transcribed all thirteen ciphered lines of f. 55 into 401 glyph tokens from native-resolution thirds.

Decoded the token stream with the calibrated key; recovered continuous French including 'sceu ce que vous avez descouvert', 'du mariage', 'vostre advis', 'd'iceulx en mon intention', 'ayt tenu ce chemin', 'entendu ce que le', 'vous mist en avant, qui l'avoit', 'l'avancement du concile, a ce que', 'de ce concile, mais nous', 'avoir l'utilite qui en sortira', 'que vous avez oy', 'par lettres'.

The reading is consistent with the clear text framing it (Catherine answers Rennes' letter of 18 June) and with the situation: the Council of Trent's closing sessions and the Habsburg marriage negotiation are enciphered while the Havre-de-Grace news in the same letter is left in clear.

Prior-solution status changed from 'no' to 'partial'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page's inference 'so the passage had never been read' was withdrawn.
Fetched native-resolution IIIF crops of 500 Colbert 390 p.357 (view 180), p.139 and the glossed p.138 (view 70), 500 Colbert 392 p.231 (view 112) and its clear end p.232 (view 113).
Wrote lattice.py: beam decoder over per-glyph candidate values under the fr-1530-despatches model (lang/), so homophone choices are made by the language model, not by eye.

Colbert 390 p.357: 15 cipher lines transcribed and decoded with lattice.py; read nearly end to end ('il fauldra prandre autre pretexte… laisser là quelque secretaire… soubz couleur d'aucuns voz affaires particuliers').
Colbert 390 p.139, first two attempts with generous null options: the LM produced fluent nonsense; nothing secure.
Colbert 390 p.138 (same hand as p.139): aligned its contemporary margin decipherment against the cipher; fixed ℌ=r, ƀ=e, ſſ=o, 9=m/n, z=a/p, ⊥⊥=pour, ca=faire for this hand.

Colbert 390 p.139: fresh transcription from contrast-enhanced crops with the p.138 values, five passes; about 36% secure, 27% probable ('que je vous tienne pour trop advisé et affectionné et loyal serviteur du roy mon fils… les yeux ouverts pour observer… beau frère').

Colbert 392 p.231 (Bourdin to Rennes): six passes with hand-specific values (ꝛ=p, looped ʒ=r, +=f, N=l, W=ss, ‡‡=et, δ=con, ‖=plus); about 80% read, incl. the whole closing 'd'amitié et alliance… repos de la chrestienté'.
Colbert 392 p.232 carries the clear end of the same letter, dated Paris, December 1562, signed Bourdin; 'faire changer d'opinion' echoes the cipher's 'changer d'advis et conseil'.

La Ferrière, Lettres de Catherine de Médicis I-II, and Tomokiyo searched for cribs: none of the four passages is printed. Bourdin's enclosure is Catherine to Rennes, 15 Dec 1562 (LF I 448-451); p.357's precedence dispute is summer 1564 (LF II 199-201, 216-217). Parallels in cribs.md.
fr. 3181 f.55 re-transcribed from native-resolution crops and decoded with lattice.py; secure share rose from about 55% to 75%.

Aligned the margin decipherments of fr. 3181 f.57 and f.58 (same hand as f.55) sign by sign (fr3181_glossed.md): ᑲ=e (never s), ʃʃ=le, ‡̲=con, u̲=pour, ∠=vous; f.55 now about 80% secure, 11% probable. The f.57 margin reads 'par France', not 'par Ferrare'.

Harvested glossed passages elsewhere in Colbert 390 (pp.189/199, 221-231, 241; colbert390_glossed.md): N=l, ♯=y, €=f, plain ℊ=u, ‖=plus, pl=bien, h=b; the other signs blocking p.139 and c392 occur in no gloss found. pp.241-305 are in the f.52 hand, not f.55's.

p.139 re-run with the glossed values withdrew four earlier readings (passeront, fault; laisseray and cousin downgraded) and added four (loyal, qu'il vault, ouverts, afin): a check that earlier readings were not forced.
Colbert 390 p.358 (view 181) found to continue p.357's cipher (10 lines): transcribed and read with the same values; p.357 open run read with ꭓ=u from p.358. Letter now ~99% (88% secure).

Full decipherments aligned: Colbert 390 p.317/p.313 (ẟ=com, W=ss, π=h, Ꝫ=p) and p.117-118/p.120-121 (ẟ+superscript = code word, ẟa=Allemaigne; 7=nous; ⊥⊥=pour); 1564 glossed pp.339-349 (∂ˡ=Metz). Applied to p.139 (~65%) and Colbert 392 (~85%).

Surveyed sister volumes 500 Colbert 391, 394, 395 (Bochetel correspondence series) for deciphered Rennes-cipher passages: none; only a Tournon 1557 cipher and a Boistaillé 1561 figure cipher, both undeciphered. Colbert 396, 393 and fr. 3180/3182 not surveyed.

Checked how the 0.87 figure was made: it was a hand estimate of secure+probable shares per letter, not a count, and 'probable' included words forced by one unsupported sign value or filled from context. Wrote measure.py: every token is aligned to an explicit word-by-word reading (aligned/*.txt) using only the token's candidate values; a reading the signs do not give fails to align; probable words ({n} with ~) and unread runs are counted separately; sense words are checked against a 16th-c. French vocabulary (fr-1520s-diplomatic + fr-henri4). Strict sense share before this pass: 0.72 (f.55 0.80, pp.357 0.79, p.358 0.76, c392 0.73, p.139 0.53).

p.139 re-checked sign by sign on fresh native IIIF crops (hi2/p139w.jpg): l.9 'ẟar' is a struck-out word, not a code word; l.8 '€' before cousin is ℒ (null) followed by the m-like c (ℒ m ſſ µ ¢ m aı = cousin); l.7 opens ᵐ C Ꝫ x1 = c o m e (Ꝫ = Tomokiyo's d3 = m); l.9 end is x1 not mJ; l.11 has a 9 the v3 transcription missed. Tokens saved as c390_p139_v4.txt.

p.139 new readings from v4 and ÿ = d (Tomokiyo's script-v-dot): 'pour vous en dormir bien' (l.3, ÿ ſſ ʓ ℊ m ʓ = d o r m i r), 'come totes ... passeront en ce' (l.7, ƀ = p as in the key), 'mon cousin' secure, 'encores que je n'en visse aucunement a doubter' (l.9-10), 'de vostre' before the ẟao code word (l.13). p.139 strict sense 0.53 -> 0.70.

Colbert 390 p.357 re-checked on native crops (hi2/p357w.jpg): l.14 '9 la' and l.15 'Vb' had been doubled at the half-line crop join; l.14 yy is the gamma-loop d. 'de deniers ... envoye querir' now aligns. p.357 0.79 -> 0.82.

Colbert 392 p.231 re-checked on native crops (hi2/c392a.jpg, c392b.jpg): l.1 opens ℒ ꝺ k xy = (nulls) ie; l.5 'ſ W xy u ʒ d ℌ' = asseurer and 'G C u eτ d' = toute; l.6 the sign in pro_re is the 6-shaped b = p; l.9 '€' = ẽ = ff (difficulte); l.10 'ıō xy' = ie, not w; raised small z = a in s[a]ns (l.13), y [a]voit (l.14), [a]u repos (l.25); dʒ = mm in femme and commun; l.22 the ff-ligature a in aliance. c392 0.73 -> 0.83.

Tried and failed on p.139: l.4 run 'ſ mJ z ʓ G k ẓ ƀ' (no word with a/m/p/r/t/i/e), l.8 'ſ λ ſſ ♯ z k ß', l.12 'ẟao ſ 9' and l.13-14 ẟao + 'ʓ k 9 ẓ m io ʓ η ſ ß x1' (princi[pal]e needs ʓ = p and an r the signs lack), 'choses' (needs € = h, which the € in afin and cousin contradict), 'donner'/'de me' (‡‡ and ℊ values unsupported). f.55 l.1-2 openings and l.4/8/9 runs re-viewed on native crops (hi2/f55w.jpg): no new value.

Surveyed every view of 500 Colbert 393 (198 views), 500 Colbert 396 (135), BnF fr. 3180 (120) and fr. 3182 (144) on Gallica by 12-view contact sheets, candidates opened: no cipher in the Rennes key or any other, no gloss, decipherment or key sheet (sister_volumes.md). The whole Bochetel series (Colbert 390-396) and fr. 3180-3182 are now negative; no crib, measurement unchanged at 0.79.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's published reconstruction of the Bishop of Rennes' cipher (cryptiana henryiii.htm) was applied, with per-hand letter forms taken from the glossed sibling letters (fr. 3181 ff. 57-58, Colbert 390) and an LM lattice to resolve homophones and word-like nulls.

outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py over aligned/f55.txt, p357.txt, p358.txt, c392.txt, p139.txt: cipher tokens aligned to the word-by-word reading by their candidate values; only non-probable words counted (nulls go with the following word). 2308 tokens: sense 0.79, probable 0.15, unread 0.06. Per letter: f.55 0.80, p.357 0.82, p.358 0.76, c392 0.83, p.139 0.70.
outcome.notes: Four letters in the Bishop of Rennes' cipher, each in its own secretary's hand; values calibrated per hand on contemporary glossed siblings. The earlier 0.87 was an estimate of secure+probable; measured strictly (5 Oct 2026, measure.py) the share of tokens read as sense is 0.79 after a native-resolution re-transcription pass (0.72 before it). Probable readings (15%) need a sign value no gloss or key attests; unread (6%) are code words and runs no value closes.
